correctness.rationale: Scaling u to1 gives greedy gap g in {0,1,2,3}, competitor signed gap d in Z. The displayed nonnegative 24-entry potential P(g,|d|) supported on |d|<=5 satisfies 3|g-v|-5|d±v|+P(|g-v|,d±v)<=P(g,d) by exhaustive finite g=0..3, |d|<=8, v=1,2,3, signs± checks. For |d|>=9 both potential entries vanish, |d±v|>=6 and 3g’<=9<5*6; hence all integer states covered. Telescoping from P(0,0)=0 and final nonnegative potential proves G<=5O/3 for ANY comparison allocation, all m. The repeated (1,1,3,1)(2,3,1)^r yields greedy cost 6+5r, feasible competitor cost 4+3r, so asymptotic ratio at least5/3. Independent exhaustive transition checks d in [-30,30] and exact small-sequence DP and witness family agree; infinite proof rests on full transition analysis.

value.rationale: Sharp universal online-to-offline cumulative-envy price for the first three-valued alphabet beyond two-valued greedy exactness, with a concrete recurring obstruction and a global potential. Exact general-in-horizon guarantee rather than isolated tiny numeric gain.

final_claim: For two identical positive additive agents receiving a fixed-order list of values from {u,2u,3u}, assigning each item to the lower-valued current bundle yields sum of absolute prefix imbalances G <= (5/3) times the offline optimum O. Sharp as sequence (1,1,3,1)+(2,3,1)^r grows.
limitations: Exactly two agents, identical additive valuations, positive values in three-level alphabet.
Fixed-order sequential allocation; ratio supremum asymptotic, not asserted for every finite horizon.
